changes: UI framework changed from WPF-UI to Avalonia to enable cross platform compatibility.

Changed when the program checks for conflicting participant information. It now happens whenever a participant change is detected while on the participants page, or when the participant page is loaded.
Added a link to the help documents folder to the about page.
Updated the links on the about page removing the links to no longer used packages and adding the new packages that are used.
Added the ability to link chips in reverse order, that is bibs can count down while chips count up.
DNF entries can now be listed as having a location attached to keep track of where a runner dropped.
There is now a switch to show every linked distance or just the main distances for bib pickup numbers on the participants page and the finished/active/dns stats on the timing page.

Downloading participants from the API has a minor overhaul. It now adds duplicates when a bib conflict on a single person is detected instead of clobbering information and it will add a distance if it doesn't recognize the distance.
Added a prompt confirming the user wants to delete participants from the API to ensure it wasn't an accidental button click.
Importing participants should no longer prompt when there are conflicts, it should just import them and the conflicts button should appear allowing the user to deal with it in the main UI.
The update check now ignores draft and prerelease versions.
The RFID Ultra settings window now tells you when the reader doesn't save a setting.
Errors are now written to the error log in release builds.
Stopping registration is now much quicker.

On macOS and Linux the database, logs and exports are now kept in a folder every user can use: /Users/Shared/Chronokeep on macOS and /var/lib/chronokeep on Linux. Exported files can also be opened or replaced by every user. On Linux an administrator needs to create that folder first, and the program explains how if it's missing.
Updates can now be downloaded and installed on macOS and Linux as well as Windows. On Linux the system asks for an administrator password to install the update.
Downloaded updates are now checked before they can be installed. The file has to match the release's SHA256 checksum, and GitHub has to confirm it was built by Chronokeep's release process.
Releases now include Linux packages (.deb and .rpm) and a macOS disk image (.dmg), along with SHA256 checksums and GitHub build attestations to check downloads.

Birthdates are now always stored as year/month/day (for example 1990/01/02), however they were entered or imported. Existing birthdates are converted when the database is upgraded, and participant records that only differed by how their birthdate was written are combined into one.
New timing locations now ignore repeat reads of the same runner within 10 minutes by default. Existing locations keep their current setting.

Added database support for linking an event to a Runsignup race, choosing which distance each Runsignup event goes into, and tracking participants Runsignup has removed. Removed participants won't count toward the timing page totals and their results won't be uploaded.
fixes: Disabling the automatic downloading of remote reads no longer causes the program to freeze for a number of seconds.
Fixed the issues with the 'base the running clock on this distance/wave' combobox.
Reader notification windows are no longer synchronous and should not cause reader disconnects.
Awards and Print pages have been fixed/updated to work properly and across platforms.
Fixed an issue where a secondary program would never overwrite participant information originally downloaded from the API with newer information from the API.
Changed the default dummy bib/chip from a value of '-1' to an empty string to ensure a person isn't accidentally assigned to an unknown chip read.
Fixed a silent error where the program would stop the download of participants from the api if it matched via participant information and not participant ID.
Fixed an issue where looking up a timing location or segment by its details would cause a database error.
Fixed an issue where distance stats would leave out distances that weren't linked to another distance.
Fixed an issue where distance stats could undercount participants when combining linked distances or counting DNS and unknown statuses together.
Fixed an issue where segments added one at a time wouldn't be tracked correctly until the program was restarted.
Fixed an issue where deleted age groups would continue to be used until the program was restarted.
Fixed an issue where changes to an event's name, date, start time, or results API weren't picked up until the program was restarted.
Fixed an issue where changing the start or start/finish options wouldn't fully take effect until the program was restarted.
Fixed an issue where changing a timing system's IP address would leave the old entry behind.
Fixed an issue where saving alarms could create duplicate alarms.
Fixed an issue where removing a chip from a bib could leave names attached to the wrong chip reads.
Fixed an issue where the program would keep reprocessing results when only start times were left unprocessed.
Fixed an error when banning a phone number or email that was already banned.
Fixed an issue where adding several distances at once to the open event could cause an error.
Fixed an issue where switching events could cause an error or show results with the previous event's location and segment names.
Fixed an issue where importing a participant whose address had a comma would add a leading space to the second address line.
Fixed an issue where linked distances weren't ranked using their ranking order in distance based events.
Fixed an issue where removing a chip from a bib wasn't picked up by results processing until the program was restarted, which could leave a runner marked as DNS.
Fixed an issue in backyard ultras where a start read exactly at the end of the start window was counted as a loop finish.
Fixed an issue in backyard ultras where a runner who never finished their first loop was marked DNF on the second loop.
Fixed an issue in backyard ultras where chips not assigned to a bib were marked DNF after their first loop.
Fixed an issue in backyard ultras where DNF results for known participants weren't linked to the participant.
Fixed a potential crash in backyard ultras when processing a DNF for a loop that had been started but not finished.
Fixed an issue where every read from an IPICO reader was marked as a rewind read.
Fixed an issue where reads from an IPICO reader with a reader ID containing a letter were dropped.
Fixed an issue where a DNS result would stop all results from uploading until the program was restarted. DNS results are now uploaded as DNS.
Fixed an issue where databases from older versions of the program couldn't be upgraded.
Fixed several issues with CSV imports: an extra blank column was shown, quoted values kept a trailing space, and a quoted value with a comma at the end of a line was split in two.
Fixed an issue where Excel imports dropped rows after a blank row and columns after an empty column.
Fixed an issue where an alarm removed on the alarms page kept going off until the alarms were saved.
Fixed an issue where clicking Start Web could cause an error instead of showing how to allow the web server when it couldn't start.

Fixed several issues with the local results web server: viewing a runner's results could break their printable certificate, opening a certificate could replace the runner's results page, participant counts on certificates grew with every refresh, emailed certificates didn't update when results changed, and requests for missing files never got a response.
Fixed an issue where results were uploaded again on every upload cycle when the event only uploads specific distances or is a backyard ultra with DNF entries.
Fixed an issue where stopping and starting remote reads would stop downloading reads.
Fixed an issue where remote reads could be missed on computers in time zones ahead of UTC.
Fixed an issue where the announcer stopped adding runners after someone crossed the announcer mat again after the seen window.
Fixed a typo in the text message sent when a runner reaches a split.
Fixed an issue where a text message could be sent for a result that wasn't linked to a participant.
Fixed an issue where the update check could fail without saying anything if a release on GitHub wasn't named with a version number.
Fixed an issue where certificate links in results emails were broken when a name, event, or distance had a character like '/' or '#' in it.
Fixed an issue where printable certificates showed a made-up pace when the distance had no length set. The pace is now left blank.
Fixed an issue where a reader connected at the same time another reader disconnected might never be read.
Fixed an issue where settings changed on an RFID Ultra from the reader settings window were sent without the ending character the Ultra expects.
Fixed an issue where setting a reader's time sent an invalid time on computers using a language that separates hours and minutes with a '.', such as Danish or Finnish.
Fixed an issue where setting an IPICO reader to a specific time set it to the current time instead.
Fixed the RFID Ultra channel number and antenna 4 backup commands so they match the Ultra's manual.
Fixed an issue where alarm sounds wouldn't play if the program was started from a different folder, such as from a shortcut or the macOS Finder.
Fixed an issue where printouts for time based events combined people who share a name.
Fixed an issue where an overall award winner could be skipped for their age group award, giving it to someone slower.
Fixed an issue where custom award winners were listed in their age group instead of the custom group.
Fixed an issue where award age groups were printed in the wrong order, such as 5-9 after 10-19.
Fixed an error when printing awards for a distance with no award winners.
Fixed an issue where adding or updating several participants at once from the registration app didn't send the new list to the other connected registration apps.
Fixed an issue where the check for a database moved to a different computer never ran.
Fixed an issue where stopping registration always logged an error.
Fixed an issue where text message alerts were marked as sent when texting wasn't set up, so they were never sent once it was.
Fixed an issue where the buttons on the About page for opening the data and logs folders did nothing on macOS.
Fixed an issue where saving results or awards as a PDF failed when the folder had a space in its name.
Fixed an issue on Windows where saving results or awards as a PDF failed if the program was started from a different folder, such as from a shortcut.
Fixed an issue where downloading participants from the API added a duplicate person when their birthdate was written differently, such as 01/02/1990 and 1/2/1990.
Fixed an issue where the update check could fail with an error instead of saying GitHub couldn't be reached when the connection timed out.
Fixed an issue where removing a results API left the open event linked to it until the program was restarted.
Fixed an issue where editing a participant cleared their checked in status, what they owe, their other notes and their text alert setting, and marked them as changed even when nothing was edited.
Fixed an error when opening a participant with no birthdate in the participant window.
Fixed an issue where the Change button in the change event window stayed disabled after clearing a search that matched no events.
Fixed an issue where the Reset Database and Rebuild Database buttons on the settings page did nothing after clicking Yes.
Fixed an issue where the Reset button on the locations page didn't undo unsaved changes.
Fixed an issue where clicking Update on the locations page, or leaving it, recalculated results and cleared uploaded results even when nothing had changed. Renaming a location no longer does either.
Fixed an issue where locations without an ignore within time showed it blank instead of 00:00:00.
Fixed an issue where leaving the age groups or segments page recalculated results and cleared uploaded results even when nothing had changed.
Fixed an issue where deleted or cleared ignored chips kept being ignored until the program was restarted.
Fixed an issue where clicking Delete on the chip assignment page with nothing selected recalculated results and cleared uploaded results when leaving the page.

Fixed an issue where setting a wave start as a time of day saved the wrong start offset when its milliseconds were less than the race start's, and where a wave starting just before the race start showed the wrong time of day.
Fixed an issue where a manual entry could be added without a bib.
Fixed an issue where changing the distance of several participants at once could be undone by the next download of participants from the API.
Fixed an issue where the ignore, DNS, DNF and shift buttons on the raw reads page recalculated results even when no reads were selected.
Fixed an issue where ignoring the chip of a manual entry added a blank chip to the ignored chips list, and ignoring a chip twice listed it twice.

Fixed an issue where saving an event to a file stopped partway through and left out its results, and where importing an event could use the open event's start time and locations for the imported reads.
Fixed an issue where changing the sort or searching on the participants page showed participants from every distance even when one distance was selected.
Fixed an issue where the Manual Upload button could stay stuck on Uploading after an upload failed or when the event wasn't linked to a results API.
Fixed an issue where the Registration button on the dashboard showed Stop Registration even when registration failed to start.
Fixed an issue where importing a participant file without a distance column ignored the distance chosen for it and added an unused Default Distance.
Fixed an issue where importing a bib for someone already entered without one didn't save the bib.
Fixed an issue where importing bib and chip pairs replaced chips already linked to a different bib without asking, and added pairs with a blank bib or chip.
Fixed an issue where custom timing log imports never imported anything, and where a log whose first line held column names failed to import.
Fixed an issue where Abbott WMM exports put each runner's last name in the first name column and their first name in the last name column.

Fixed an issue where RunSignup, UltraSignup, Abbott WMM and Boston exports left the gender blank for events using Male/Female. All four now write M, F or X, including X for non-binary runners in Abbott WMM exports.
Fixed an issue where UltraSignup, Abbott WMM and Boston exports wrote dates of birth in the computer's date format instead of MM/DD/YYYY.
Fixed an issue where custom award groups outside ages 0 to 100, or with the start age after the end age, could be added.
Fixed an issue where exporting results left out runners whose bib wasn't registered to a participant.
Fixed an error when saving a CSV export with an empty value, such as a place for someone who hasn't finished.
Fixed an issue where setting a reader to a specific time could use today's date instead of the date chosen.
Fixed an issue where the Chronokeep Portal settings window showed the wrong volume on computers that use a comma for decimals.
Fixed an issue where changing the screen type in the Chronokeep Portal settings window wasn't saved to the portal.
Fixed an issue where the Chronokeep Portal settings window closed by itself after a save failed because of an invalid read window.
Fixed an issue where saving an RFID Ultra setting before choosing a value sent a setting to the reader anyway.

Fixed an issue where the changelog, license, reader notifications, web print settings, clock, text message and remote readers windows could stay open after closing Chronokeep, keeping the program running.
Fixed an issue where removing a saved reader in safe mode didn't delete it, so it came back the next time.
Fixed an issue where setting all readers' times in safe mode also tried readers that weren't connected, and stopped at the first one that failed.
Fixed an issue where the web print settings accepted negative margins or a scale of zero or less.
Fixed an issue where Chronoclock times were sent in the wrong format on computers that don't use a colon between hours and minutes.
Fixed an issue where a failed lock or brightness change left a Chronoclock's controls unusable until refreshed, and showed the lock as changed.
Fixed an issue where refreshing a Chronoclock sent its brightness back to it.
Fixed an issue where a Chronoclock didn't show the event's start time when the race started before 10:00.
Fixed an issue where one remote API that couldn't be reached closed the Remote Readers window, hiding the readers on every other remote API.
Fixed an issue where Chronokeep Portal reader antennas weren't colored green or red until the reader itself changed.
Fixed an issue where saving a Chronokeep Portal reader with an invalid IP address or port saved it with a blank address or port 0 instead of refusing.
Fixed an issue where switching off a Chronokeep Portal reader that was connected but not reading started it instead of stopping it.
Fixed an issue where the text message window showed a wave as on when only some of its distances were, and Set left the others unchanged.
Fixed an issue where no messages or confirmations were shown in safe mode.

Fixed an issue where removing a distance whose linked distances had participants removed only one linked distance on Yes, removed linked distances without participants even on No, and left removed distances showing until the page was reopened.
Fixed an issue where the tag tester numbered reads on from where the last tag tester window left off instead of starting at 1.
Fixed an issue where safe mode couldn't be closed while timing was running, because answering Yes to the exit question didn't close it.
Fixed an issue where backing up the database a second time on the same day from the update window failed.
Fixed an issue where rewinding an Ipico reader never asked the reader to replay its reads.
Fixed an issue where the Rewind window closed as soon as an Ipico rewind was asked about, instead of staying open and busy until the rewind finished.
Fixed an issue where reads from an Ipico rewind weren't scored until another read came in.
Fixed an issue where an Ipico rewind could wait a long time on a reader that couldn't be reached or stopped sending.

Fixed an issue where boxes meant for numbers, IP addresses or chips accepted any typing, including the reader IP and port, age group ages, distance, wave and rank, location occurrences, segment distances, award counts, chip numbers and Chip Tool ranges.
Fixed an issue where pressing Enter in the race start time box started the clock but didn't save the start time or recalculate results until the box lost focus.
Fixed an issue where the participant window opened from the timing results could stay open after closing Chronokeep, keeping the program running.
Event dates are now stored as year/month/day, the same as birthdates, so a database reads the same on every computer. The database upgrade rewrites existing event dates.
Printouts and the safe mode window show the event date written out, such as June 15, 2026.
Boston exports write the event date as MM/DD/YYYY, like their dates of birth.

Fixed an issue where event dates could be saved in a form that computers using a different date format, including the one that saved it, couldn't read, which broke start times, ages and results for that event.
Fixed an issue where RFID Ultra low battery warnings never appeared on computers that use a comma for decimals.
Fixed an issue where two-digit birth years such as 45 were read as 2045 instead of 1945, and where a birthdate after the event gave a negative age.
Participants removed from registration keep their results but no longer take an overall, gender, age group or division place, so the places of everyone else have no gaps.
Fixed an issue where a runner marked DNF after being placed kept their division place.
Fixed an issue where only a backyard ultra runner's latest loop showed their division place.
The Change Event list shows each event's date written out, such as June 15, 2026.
Fixed an issue where timing stopped scoring reads for good after one failed pass, or after the open event was deleted, until Chronokeep was restarted.
Fixed an issue where automatic result uploads stopped for good after one failed pass.
Fixed an issue where changes made while timing was busy for a long time were saved but didn't show until the event was reopened.
Fixed an issue where accented names in CSV files saved in the Windows encoding imported as garbled characters.
Fixed an issue where dates and decimal numbers imported from Excel files depended on the computer's date and number format.
Fixed an issue where a spreadsheet or CSV row with fewer columns than the header broke the import.
Fixed an issue where pasting into boxes meant for numbers, IP addresses or chips let any text in.
Added Runsignup as an API type. Add it on the Manage API page with its API key and secret.

Added Link to Runsignup on the Dashboard. It links the event to a Runsignup race, sets the distance for each Runsignup event (or skips it), and chooses the race questions and fields copied into Comments for the announcer. When a race's name and date match the event, it's picked out ready to confirm. Only the race's events nearest the event's date are shown, since Runsignup lists every year's events.

Added a Runsignup Download button on the Participants page. It downloads this year's participants, with their apparel from the giveaway (such as Long Sleeve Shirt (Large)), registration add-ons (such as T-Shirt (Small)) and race store, and their chips, then shows how many were downloaded. Choices that say no, such as No shirt or None, are left out.
Participants removed in Runsignup are left out of the timing counts and result uploads. They stay on the Participants page and the results page, tinted red with the reason.

For participants removed in Runsignup, the participant window shows why (Transferred, Deferred, Cleared, Removed) with a switch beside the distance. Switching it off puts them back in the race, and later downloads won't remove them again.
The bib stats on the Participants page count removed participants who still hold a bib in a new Removed column.
Added a Test button to every API on the Manage API page. It checks the API can be reached with the values typed in.

The Participants page's Download and Upload buttons show their progress, such as Page 2 or 250 / 1000, instead of Working, and the number of participants downloaded or uploaded shows under them afterwards.
The Manual Upload button on the timing page shows how many results have been uploaded so far.
Fixed an issue where removing a participant from an event also removed them from every other event they were in.
Fixed an issue where starting Chronokeep while another copy was open crashed with a closed window error instead of saying Chronokeep is already running.
Fixed an issue where Chronokeep stopped responding while participants downloaded from Chronokeep or Runsignup were being saved.

The announcer is now a web page instead of a window, so any computer or tablet on the network can show it. The Announcer button turns it on and off, starting the web server if it isn't running. The page is at /announcer on the web address shown on the Timing page.

The announcer page shows runners read at the announcer location and runners crossing the finish line together in one list, with how long ago each was first seen. A runner read at the announcer location who then finishes within the Repeat Window shows once, and with a Repeat Window of 0 each runner only shows once. The Time column shows their finish time once they've finished.

The announcer page has a settings pane for making the text larger or smaller, choosing which columns show, showing unknown runners (bibs that were read but that nobody is registered with) and showing a running clock for each distance along the bottom. Settings are kept separately on each device.
Fixed an issue where the web address link on the Timing page didn't open, and showed localhost instead of the network address on computers connected by Wi-Fi.
Fixed an issue where turning the announcer on, or starting the web server, froze Chronokeep until it had started.
Fixed an issue where restarting the announcer could leave the old one running alongside the new one, so runners could be listed twice.
Removed the Restart Announcer Worker button from the Dashboard. Turning the announcer off and on again restarts it.
When the web server can't start, the command it shows now also adds a firewall rule, so other computers and tablets on the network can reach it.
The announcer list is built once and shared by every device showing the announcer page, so having several open doesn't slow Chronokeep down.
Anonymous runners show as Anonymous on the announcer page, without their city, state or comments.
